CHAPTER 1: PRELIMINARIES
1.1. Authority
In exercising the powers conferred to the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan (hereinafter
referred to as "the Authority") under Section 167 and 171 of the Financial Services Act 2011, the
Board of the Authority hereby adopts the Penalty (Amendment) Regulations.These regulations
establish the principles and methodologies for determining and imposing administrative penalties
on any individuals or Financial Services Providers (hereinafter referred to as “FSPs”) that violate
any provisions of the rules, regulations, guidelines, directives, and notifications issued by the
Authority from time to time.
1.2. Scope and Objective
The Authority plays a critical role in maintaining the safety, soundness, and stability of the
financial system in the interest of the nation. To fulfill this mandate, the Authority shall take
timely and appropriate action against any individuals or FSPs that fail to comply with the
regulatory requirements.
The objective of these regulations is to provide broad provisions for assessing and
imposing monetary and administrative penalties, mainly to:
a) reinforce the integrity and credibility of FSPs by ensuring that violations are
swiftly identified, strictly monitored, and penalized with severity commensurate to
the breach;
b) guarantee that enforcement actions are not only proportionate but also firm,
predictable, and uniformly applied; and
c) deter individuals and FSPs from contravening any rules, regulations, guidelines,
directives, and notifications, issued by the Authority.
1.3. Title, Commencement, and Application
This Regulations shall:
(a) Be called the Penalty (Amendment) Regulations 2025;
(b) Come into force from July 2025 and;
(c) Shall apply to:
i. All the FSPs licensed, registered, or authorized by the Authority.
ii. Any individual who is governed by regulations which are framed and enforced
by the Authority.
3

1.4. Repeal and Saving
Upon adoption of the amended regulations by the Board of the Authority:
(a) The Penalty Rules and Regulations 2022 shall stand repealed;
(b) Supersede any directive, circular, guidelines, references or notifications that are
inconsistent with these regulations; and
(c) All actions taken by the Authority under the Penalty Rules and Regulations 2022
shall stand until appropriate remedies or rectifications are carried out by the FSPs.
1.5. Interpretation
The Authority shall interpret any provision of these regulations, and its interpretation shall
be final and binding on any individuals or FSPs.
CHAPTER 2: VIOLATIONS AND PROCEDURES FOR DETERMINING
ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS OR MONETARY PENALTIES
2.1. Violations
The Authority shall consider violations eligible for monetary penalties and/or
administrative sanctions including, but not limited to, the following:
(a) Violation of the rules, regulations, guidelines, or directives issued by the Authority;
(b) Non-compliance with the observations/findings/corrective actions within the
timeline prescribed by the Authority;
(c) Contraventions that are tantamount to offence and not covered by these regulations;
and
(d) Notwithstanding the above provisions, offences that are clearly stipulated with a
penalty in the Acts shall be dealt with as per the provisions of the respective Acts.
2.2. Penalty Assessment Criteria
In determining the monetary penalty, the Authority must consider a wide range of factors to
ensure that it arrives at a fair and proportionate amount that reflects the gravity of the
violation and the circumstances of each case. The factors include, but are not limited, to the
following:
(a) Severity of the violation(s);
(b) Intent and negligence;
(c) Frequency of violations;
(d) Remedial actions taken;
(e) Effectiveness of internal control and compliance management systems; and
(f) Financial impact.
4

2.3. Procedures for Imposing Penalty and Timeline
The Authority shall administer the following procedures sequentially and the specified
timeline to identify and impose a monetary penalty and/or administrative sanction(s) on any
individual or FSP.
(a) Identification and Assessment of Violation(s)
(i) The department(s) concerned shall identify the violation(s) through its oversight,
monitoring and other supervisory and surveillance mechanism;
(ii) The department(s) concerned shall document its recommendations and workout
the completed Penalty Matrix (refer to Annexure A) along with the supporting
documents to determine the kind of enforcement action required;
(iii) The department(s) concerned shall complete the Penalty Matrix in accordance
with provisions of Chapter 3 to ensure that the penalty is imposed consistently and
equitably; and
(iv) The findings and recommendations along with the necessary supporting
documents shall be submitted to the Legal Services Division for consultation.
(v) The relevant department, in collaboration with the Legal Services Division, shall
present the matter to the Executive Committee (hereinafter referred to as the
Committee) for the final determination on the imposition of monetary penalty and/or
administrative sanction.
(b) Written Notice
If the Committee decides to impose a penalty (monetary and/or administrative
sanction) on the FSP or an individual, the decision shall be communicated through a
written notice. The written notice, among other things, shall include the following:
(i) Seek explanation for the violation(s) within a 14 working day period in
accordance with Section 157 of the FSA 2011, from the date of issuance of the
notice; and
(ii) Inform the intent of the Authority to impose appropriate penalties stating
specifically the legal and factual grounds upon which it is based.
(iii) Provide an opportunity to submit additional documentary evidence to the
Authority for review and consideration of the penalties as per the timelines set
out.
5

(c) Penalty or No-Penalty Order
Based on the receipt/non-receipt of explanations within 14 working days, the Committee
shall decide the next course of action.
(i) If satisfactory explanations not to impose monetary penalties are furnished, the
Committee may impose any of the administrative sanctions mentioned in Section
2.4. via the Legal Services Division.
(ii) In the event, the Committee is not satisfied with the explanations furnished by
the concerned FSP or the individual, the Authority may impose the following;
a. For FSPs: a Penalty Order specifying the amount, determined based on the
penalty matrix. The Penalty Order may also include corrective actions with
specific timelines for compliance and rectification.
b. For individuals: a monetary penalty not exceeding the equivalent of one
year’s daily minimum wage may be imposed for any violation, subject to the
Authority’s discretion to determine an appropriate amount based on the
factors outlined in Section 2.2. In the case of repeated offenders, the
Authority may impose a monetary penalty and/or administrative sanctions,
and the one year’s daily minimum wage cap shall not necessarily be
applicable.
2.4. Supervisory Powers and Enforcement Actions
The Authority may impose monetary penalty and/or any of the following administrative
sanction on the FSPs and individuals for non-compliance with regulatory requirements,
where applicable, after taking into account the factors outlined in Section 2.2:
(a) Written warnings/letter of advice;
(b) Suspension or revocation of license;
(c) Restriction on business activities or prohibition of specific financial services;
(d) Additional capital charge; or
(e) Any other necessary enforcement measures the Authority deems fit.
2.5. Appeal mechanism
(i) Pursuant to Section 162 of the FSA 2011, the concerned FSP or individual may appeal in
writing to the Authority’s Board within 14 working days from the date on which any
monetary and/or administrative sanction is imposed.
(ii) The Board of the Authority shall affirm, reverse, modify or maintain the status quo of
the decision and state its legal and factual grounds.
(iii) An appeal against the Board’s decision may be filed within 21 working days with a
court of law that has jurisdiction over the FSP or the individual.
6

2.6. Enforcement of Penalty
(i) The penalty imposed on the individual or the FSPs shall be payable to the Authority
within a period of 30 working days from the date of issuing the Penalty Order.
(ii) If the FSP maintains a current account with the Authority, the Department of Banking
shall debit the penalty amount from the FSP’s account upon receiving an order from the
Legal Services Division, provided that the FSP does not file an appeal within 14 working
days.
(iii)The Department of Banking shall maintain a specific account for this purpose.
(iv) For those without an account with the Authority, the penalty may be paid in cash or
through a formal banking channel. Proof of payment must be provided through a receipt,
bank transfer confirmation, or any other verifiable payment instrument, such as a deposit
slip or electronic payment record.
(v) In case of failure in payment of penalty amount, the Authority shall initiate appropriate
action to impose an additional penalty not exceeding twice the amount of the penalty as per
Section 168 of FSA 2011.
2.7. Public Statement
The concerned Department(s) may, following the issuance of a Penalty Order, disclose the
name of the FSP, the amount of the penalty, and the nature of the violation on its official
website or through other appropriate media channels.
CHAPTER 3: PENALTY CALCULATION AND METHODOLOGY
3.1. Number of Matrices
One matrix shall be completed for one FSP for all or one violation. When there are several
violations included in one matrix, the highest severity level applicable for any of them will
be recorded for each factor in the matrix.
3.2. Explanation of the Factors
(a) Concealment: This factor considers the extent to which the violation or relevant
facts were concealed. It includes situations where there was no concealment and
the misconduct was voluntarily self-disclosed; where disclosure occurred only
upon request by the Authority or another relevant body; and where the FSP
actively took steps to conceal the misconduct or material facts from the Authority,
auditors, or other regulatory bodies.
(b) Repetition of violation in the last five years: This factor considers whether the FSP
has committed the same violation within the last five years. It distinguishes
7

between three levels of recurrence: (i) no repetition, where the violation is a
first-time occurrence within the five-year period; (ii) a single repetition, where the
same violation has occurred once within the last five years. Any prior occurrence
outside this five-year window is not considered under this factor, and (iii) multiple
repetitions, where the same violation has been committed more than once within
the same timeframe, indicating a recurring compliance failure or disregard for
regulatory requirements. For example, a previous Capital Adequacy Ratio
requirement violation and a current Capital Adequacy Ratio requirement violation.
(c) Duration and frequency of violation(s) before Written Notice: This factor assesses
the length of time and frequency with which a violation or non-compliant practice
occurred prior to the issuance of a written notice by the Authority. It includes: (i)
isolated violations, where the conduct was infrequent or occurred as a single
instance over a short period; (ii) repeated or sustained violation(s) lasting up to one
year, where the same or similar violation(s) occurred multiple times or were
ongoing for a period not exceeding one year; and (iii) prolonged violation(s)
exceeding one year, where the conduct persisted for more than one year prior to
regulatory detection or intervention, reflecting a sustained failure to comply with
regulatory requirements. Under severity level 2, “practice” includes if the conduct
of violations is prescribed in the FSP’s internal policies and procedures. This factor
does not assess prior resolved violations but focuses solely on the duration and
frequency of the conduct leading up to the current enforcement action.
(d) Continuation after Written Notice: this factor refers to a formal notice issued by the
Authority to the FSP following the Authority’s determination of a violation, or
other non-compliance. Such notification shall set out the particulars of the alleged
contravention and require the FSP to provide an explanation within the period
specified by the Authority.
(e) Impact on financial stability/systemic risk/reputational risk/public service: No
impact means there is no effect on financial stability/systemic risk/reputational risk
or on the public service delivery. An indirect impact suggests secondary effects
through market or institutional connections, while a direct impact poses an
immediate threat, potentially triggering a crisis within the FSP or the entire
financial system.
(f) Financial gain or loss to the FSP as a result of violation: Includes any direct or
indirect monetary gain or loss to the FSP.
8

(g) Impact or harm other than the financial loss to the FSP: Impact or harm other than
financial loss can be any possible negative impact or harm such as increased
reputational risk, operational risk, or compliance risk to the FSP. It can also include
harm to consumers or to the public resulting from the violation(s).
(h) Effectiveness of Internal Controls and compliance management systems: This
factor is to evaluate whether and how the FSP’s internal controls or compliance
programs, or lack thereof, contributed to the violation or deficiency in question.
Internal control systems or compliance management programs that are so lacking
as to permit the violation to occur and remain undetected should be accorded the
most severe score. Internal control systems or compliance programs that identified
the violation or deficiency, which allowed the FSP to initiate timely corrective
measures, may receive a lower score.
CHAPTER 4: MISCELLANEOUS
4.1. Amendment and Review
The Authority reserves the right to amend or review these regulations, including the penalty
matrix, as and when necessary, in response to development in the financial sector and the broader
economy.
4.2. Definitions
In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires;
(a) Acts refer to Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan Act of Bhutan, 2010 and
Financial Services Act of Bhutan, 2011.
(b) Authority means Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan established under Section 3
of the Royal Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan, 2010.
(c) Board means the Board of the Authority established under Section 33 of the Royal
Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan, 2010.
(d) Executive Committee means the Committee established under Section 56 of the
Royal Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan, 2010.
(e) Financial Service Providers means any person engaged in banking business,
insurance business, securities business and all other services designated in a
regulation adopted by the Authority as a financial service.
(f) Person means a natural or a juridical person.
(g) Repeated offender means an individual who has committed the same or a
substantially similar violation on more than one occasion within a five-year period.
